title: JSON Corruption Bisect Notebook — intermittent toolcall parse fail
summary: Notes from an ad-hoc bisect session to track down intermittent corrupted JSON returned by tool integrations during function/tool call handling. Repro steps, logs, hypotheses, regexes tried, and next steps.
content:
Problem statement:
- Intermittent failures when parsing tool responses from 'search_tool' adapter during function/tool calling flow. Failure mode: JSON.parse throws, downstream structured output validator rejects. Happens ~1–3% of calls in prod, higher in staging under load.

Observed symptoms (examples):
- Duplicate top-level key (same key appears twice), e.g.:
  {
    "results": [...],
    "meta": {...},
    "results": {...}  <-- duplicate, second one small and truncated
  }
- Trailing comma sometimes present: {"a":1,}
- Embedded nulls or control chars: "description": "This item\u0000was cut"
- Leading non-json junk (partial HTTP headers prepended) in rare cases
- BOM (\uFEFF) occasionally at start
- Sometimes valid JSON but mismatched schema (string instead of array)

Immediate impact:
- Runtime validation fails, triggers fallback code path which increases latency and costs (falls back to smaller model).
- Customer-visible errors in a small percentage of requests.

Quick repro attempts (staging):
- Needle: hammering search_tool concurrently with 200 qps for 10m. Reproduced ~2 failures (logs attached below).
- Single threaded run: no failures after 10k calls.
- Local dev with adapter stub (python) never reproduces.

Example failing request/response (redacted):
- Request ID: req-2026-03-11-15-02-17
- Outgoing tool payload (what we send to the adapter):
  POST /invoke HTTP/1.1
  Host: internal-tool-adapter
  Content-Type: application/json
  {
    "query": "vector search: 'small-metal'",
    "limit": 10
  }
- Response body (raw bytes, hex shown for first 64 bytes):
  0xEF 0xBB 0xBF 0x7B 0x22 0x72 0x65 0x73 0x75 0x6C 0x74 0x73 0x22 0x3A 0x5B ...
  Interpretation: starts with UTF-8 BOM (EF BB BF) then valid JSON.
- Another sample (truncated):
  "status:" 200 OK\r\n\r\n{
  "results": [ ... ],
  "meta": { ... },
  "results": {
    "count": 1
  }
}
  -> Here we see HTTP status text prepended inside the body (adapter upstream bug?).

Logs/stack traces from the parser (node runtime):
- Error: Unexpected token , in JSON at position 12345
    at JSON.parse (<anonymous>)
    at parseToolResponse (/app/services/tool-runner.js:142:22)
    at processToolCall (/app/services/call-orchestrator.js:314:18)
- Timestamps line up with adapter response timings (latency spiky at same moments).

What I tried (heuristics and quick fixes):
1) Pre-sanitize body before JSON.parse:
   - strip BOM: body = body.replace(/^[\uFEFF\u200B]+/, '')
   - trim control characters: body = body.replace(/[\u0000-\u0008\u000B-\u000C\u000E-\u001F]/g, '')
   - remove leading HTTP-like junk: body = body.replace(/^([^{\[]+)/, '')  // naive cut before first brace/bracket
   Outcome: guarded against BOM and some leading junk; reduced incidents but did not eliminate duplicate keys or partial truncation.

2) Lenient JSON parser (try/catch then use regex to pick first {...} block):
   - regex = /({[\\s\\S]*})/m; match = body.match(regex); if (match) JSON.parse(match[1]);
   Outcome: avoided a class of failures, but risky (captures wrong brace nesting when stacks contain docs with braces).

3) Validate duplicate keys: parse using a streaming parser (node 'clarinet' / python 'ijson') to detect duplicates and log them.
   Outcome: Able to detect when duplicate key appears and dump the path where it happens. On 12 failures in staging, duplicates correlate with adapter restarts.

Hypotheses:
- H1: Adapter occasionally concatenates two responses when under high concurrency due to reusing same TCP connection buffer without clearing. Evidence: some responses show two JSON blobs back-to-back or HTTP headers then JSON.
- H2: Under-memory pressure the adapter writes partial JSON and then another worker appends a second partial blob -> duplicated keys and truncation.
- H3: A sidecar (eg logging process) is injecting lines into stdout that are being forwarded into the HTTP response body in some deployments (less likely, but seen similar when running apt logging in other stacks).
- H4: Race in our function tool-runner where streaming remainder from previous call remains in buffer and is prepended to next body when using keep-alive sockets.

Bisect plan (what I ran):
- Goal: find commit/rollout that introduced higher failure rate.
- Start: staging image tag range between v2025.11.3 (low failures) and v2026.01.1 (observed first spike).
- Method: deploy midpoints, run synthetic workload (200 qps, random queries) for 20m, monitor parser-exception rate.
- Results:
  - v2025.11.3: 0 failures (baseline)
  - v2025.12.8: 0 failures
  - v2026.00.15: 5 failures /20m (small)
  - v2026.00.40: 12 failures /20m (higher)
  - v2026.01.01: 14 failures /20m
- Narrow commit range: found changes around connection pooling in tool-adapter (PR #87).

Repository clues (notes):
- PR #87 (tool-adapter): changed http client to use global agent with keepAlive=true and introduced buffered writer. Was intended to reduce tail latency (benchmarks here: github.com/redwood-inference/tool-adapter/pull/87). Suspicious.
- Related change: logging middleware now writes JSON metadata to stdout asynchronously (non-blocking). Could interleave with response if stdout is forwarded by sidecar incorrectly.

Temporary mitigations deployed to staging (fast rollback plan):
- Option A (safe): sanitize response body aggressively at the orchestrator edge (strip leading non-json, detect multiple concatenated blobs and take last blob). Pros: quick, minimal infra change. Cons: masks root cause, may still accept corrupted JSON.
- Option B (more targeted): pin tool-adapter to previous image v2025.11.3 while we debug (rollback). Pros: eliminates problem quickly. Cons: loses keep-alive perf gains.
- Deployed: Option B to a canary pool (10% of traffic) and Option A in orchestrator globally for 24hrs. Observed immediate drop of parser errors in canary; global sanitization dropped but some edge cases still appear.

Data collected (attached sample ids):
- sample-req-231: duplicate key + HTTP junk prefix (binary dump in /tmp/samples/req-231.bin)
- sample-req-412: BOM + trailing comma
- sample-req-578: embedded \u0000 in description field
- All samples uploaded to s3://redwood-debug/json-corrupt-samples/ (internal only)

Regex / heuristics tried (list):
- strip BOM: body.replace(/^\uFEFF+/, '')
- remove leading non-json: body.replace(/^[^{\[]+/, '')
- take only last JSON object if multiple: matches = body.match(/({[\\s\\S]*?})(?=[^{]*$)/g) -> take last
- drop non-ASCII except whitespace/punctuation: body.replace(/[^	
-]/g, '')  // too risky
- streaming parse to find duplicate keys and emit path (used clarinet with onkey event)

Notes on parser changes considered:
- Implement tolerant parser that returns a list of parsed top-level objects when multiple blobs are present, then validate each against schema and pick the one with highest conformance score. This could be robust but expensive.
- Add metrics to count presence of BOM, null chars, trailing commas, duplicate keys. Already added a short-term metric: tool_response_sanitizer.problem_type (labels: bom,trailing_comma,duplicate_key,embedded_null,leading_junk)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Confirm whether adapter sidecar (k8s logging) is involved. Action: replicate deployment with and without sidecar logging forwarding enabled. (Assigned to Mateo)
- Reproduce at high QPS with tcpdump to capture raw bytes and see if concatenated responses are sent on wire or merged later. (Assigned to Priya)
- Review PR #87 codepath for globalAgent reuse; instrument socket lifecycle (keep-alive reuse count, lastWriteTime). (Assign to eng-infra)
- Consider rolling back keepAlive change if root cause aligns, and re-run benchmarks to compare cost delta.

Immediate next steps (1–3 days):
- [ ] Run controlled tcpdump reproduction in staging with instrumented adapter (capture plain bytes)
- [ ] Add socket reuse metrics to adapter: activeSockets, reusedSockets, averageIdleTime
- [ ] Add more aggressive logging in adapter to dump raw body on 4xx/5xx and on parser-error (redact PII)
- [ ] Schedule a short postmortem if rollback needed for production (CS + infra)

Random notes / scribbles:
- Found small cluster where 95th p99 latency spikes correlate with parser errors — maybe transient GC in adapter? Check memory graphs.
- When using regex to cut to first brace, we sometimes lost leading array responses (like starting with '['). Need logic to handle either.
- If duplicated keys are literally two whole responses concatenated, picking the last JSON blob might be safest (assume later response is freshest). But if partial second response caused truncation, last blob could be invalid. So maybe pick largest well-formed blob by size and schema conformance.

References / past incidents:
- Similar incident in 2024 (ticket: JIRA-ENG-1998) where sidecar logging injected logs into stdout causing broken payloads; root cause then was non-buffered logger in a java service.

End of notebook.

-- ANS (notes end)
